title: NASA impact changed asteroid's shape and movement, ESA says

content:
A spacecraft deliberately crashing into the small asteroid Dimorphos has significantly changed its shape and movement, according to new images released by the European Space Agency (ESA) on Wednesday.

The side hit by NASA's DART probe in September 2022 now has a crater the size of a sports stadium, astrophysicist Patrick Michel, who was involved in the mission, said. The impact has also left the asteroid looking flatter and causing it to tumble, ESA said.

The findings could help scientists develop ways to deflect asteroids and prevent potentially devastating impacts on Earth.

Dimorphos is about 150 metres across and orbits the larger asteroid Didymos. The pair is currently about 190 million kilometres from Earth.

ESA's Hera mission is studying the effects of the DART impact. It has now provided the first high-resolution images of the altered asteroid.

The impact successfully changed Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos, shortening its orbital period by about 33 minutes to 11 hours and 23 minutes. However, scientists still need Hera's observations to assess how effective the deflection was.

The images also revealed hundreds of rocks moving around the asteroid pair, ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, said planetary scientist Naomi Murdoch, who is part of the Hera data analysis team.

Scientists do not yet know whether the debris was created by the DART impact or came from another source. The rocks could pose a risk to two small satellites that are due to land on Dimorphos as part of the mission. Researchers are now assessing whether their planned route needs to be changed.
